missionPremise: 30b_smartcity_design_system.md section 1.3 is the type law for every SmartCity surface: two faces, eight ramp steps, and a 12px floor whose single named exception is the evidence chip, a component that does not exist in this product. web/shell.css violated the floor in fourteen declarations and sat off the ramp in four more. The specific reason the serving build read flat is that .panel-head .t shipped at 620 13px/18px while body shipped at 400 14px/20px, so a section head was SMALLER than the text it headed and the page had no reading order.

howTheNavBadgeProblemWasSolved.constraintThatDecidedIt: src/ui.test.mjs asserts the exact byte sequence `>LABELSTATE` for fifteen nav rows and is owned by lane B77. Any markup solution would either break a test this lane may not edit or require editing another lane's file. So the solution had to be CSS-only.
howTheNavBadgeProblemWasSolved.mechanism: .navitem gains flex-wrap: wrap with column-gap 9px and row-gap 2px, keeps min-height 32px, and takes 6px vertical padding so it has auto height. .navitem .badge gains margin-left: auto. Flex line breaking places items by their outer hypothetical main size: the label is an anonymous flex item sized to its max-content width, the .grow spacer has flex-basis 0, so the BADGE is the item pushed to a second line, never the label, and margin-left: auto right-aligns it there.
howTheNavBadgeProblemWasSolved.whyNotTheDecorationOption: The card also offered reducing the badge to its state word without decoration. That buys about 12px, which would have fit both current overflow rows, but it fails again on the next long label and it changes the badge's shipped form. The wrap is robust to any future label length and changes nothing but type, so it was chosen.

foundAndNotFixed.finding: Interface controls (.btn, .navitem, .tabs a) sit at weight 500, which is not on the ramp at 14px; the ramp offers body at 400 and body-em at 600.

Both are vertical-alignment devices rather than text ramp steps: 30px centres the value in a 32px input, and 32px keeps the word-variant metric the same height as the numeral variant so the strip does not jump. Their sizes are on the ramp (body 14px and head 15px).

selfCaughtErrors: A verification grep for the metrics two-column rule used a string that also matched the pre-existing rule in the 900px media query, so it could never return false and reported the rule present when a CSS swap had silently reverted it. Caught by reading git diff. Re-applied and re-verified by extracting the 1180 block specifically. This is the same defect class the guard test exists to prevent, committed while writing that guard.

The measurement harness's own output block sat in normal flow and imposed a 500px minimum body width, contaminating the narrow-width comparison it was built to make. Fixed, re-measured, and the conclusion narrowed to widths the instrument can actually reach.

Two generated scripts had backslash escapes collapsed into real newlines. One failed loudly because every replacement asserts exactly one match; the other failed SILENTLY, rendering a page that reported nothing, which would have read as no-measurement-available. Both rewritten with String.fromCharCode, and the guard test now carries a CRLF fixture.
